content.outro: Wend Mere fills again in the night, as it does every year, over whatever the reckoning left.
content.premise: Once a year Wend Mere is let out through its sluice, and the Tallyhouse in its bed stands dry for a day. Its keeper, Ysolde Marrow, reckons the house before the water comes back. This year she has asked strangers to walk it first: to the callbell, to the man in the cell, to the ledger on its stand, and to do with each what they think right.
content.theme: A shrine in a drained mere, three things in it to answer for, and a keeper who reckons the house by what was done with them.
content.title: The Reckoning
